contract.task: Implement and run a bounded prompt token-ID transport probe using local cached tokenizers; evaluate user's idea without claiming model generation or KV cache savings.
context: Worktree /Users/alexey.zhuchkov/.codex/worktrees/agent-language-concept/Agents; existing delegation experiment underway. Venv Python /Users/alexey.zhuchkov/Documents/Agents/.venv/bin/python has tokenizers; tiktoken/transformers absent.

Native agent tool accepts text message, not token IDs. Packet profile should bind tokenizer SHA and render profile; input is already-rendered plain worker_context (not chat template). Hashes provide integrity binding, not authentication. Passing IDs cannot imply prompt semantics compilation.
scope: Read exact prepared context and two cached tokenizers; write probe/results/test artifacts in /private/tmp; run tiny local probes.
non_goals: No repository edits, no network/install, no model inference, no real agent token-ID messaging, no delegation, no broad tests.

acceptance_criteria.description: Produce a self-contained Python CLI /private/tmp/accord-token-probe.py using installed tokenizers, and JSON results /private/tmp/accord-token-probe-results.json on the exact text /private/tmp/accord-code-worker-context.txt.

Record tokenizer SHA256, input SHA256, encode/decode exact roundtrip, token count, UTF8/JSON IDs/uint32 bytes and zlib text bytes; use add_special_tokens=False and disable padding/truncation. Compare at least two local tokenizer profiles, reject wrong-profile artifact and tampered IDs before use.

Separate encoder transport experiment from chat model execution: cached models are embeddings, no engine inference, no billing/latency/quality claim. Include small focused tests of integrity and profile mismatch and report actual results.
Save exact required worker JSON to /private/tmp/accord-token-worker-result.json. No production writes.

result.summary: Implemented and ran a bounded local tokenizer transport probe with tokenizers 0.22.2. Both cached profiles encode the exact 15,456-byte worker context to 3,617 IDs and decode it byte-for-byte, including after serialized packet reload. Compact JSON IDs occupy 20,811 bytes; uint32 little-endian IDs occupy 14,468 bytes; zlib level 9 text occupies 6,095 bytes; zlib level 9 uint32 IDs occupy 5,622 bytes. Profile-bound JSON packets occupy 21,565 and 21,572 bytes excluding their terminal newline. Seven focused checks passed. This is an encoder/transport experiment with no model inference or agent token-ID messaging.

changes.description: Self-contained Python CLI using the installed tokenizers package, bounded input/tokenizer reads, add_special_tokens=False, disabled padding/truncation, exact UTF-8 handling, tokenizer/render profile binding, integrity validation, serialization metrics, and seven focused checks. Supports --input, --output and repeated --profile NAME=TOKENIZER_JSON overrides.
Actual measurements, SHA256 values, exact roundtrip results, check outcomes, comparison and limitations from both local tokenizer profiles.
Serialized Harrier-profile token-ID packet, reloaded and verified against the separately supplied profile and source digest.
Serialized EmbeddingGemma-profile token-ID packet, reloaded and verified against the separately supplied profile and source digest.

evidence.description: Harrier tokenizer SHA256 ec95be298bea26f90370854faa650744c9fb0a04ca5e5ff95dd3913393ac5e45; EmbeddingGemma tokenizer SHA256 4dda02faaf32bc91031dc8c88457ac272b00c1016cc679757d1c441b248b9c47. Both profiles report exact encode/decode and persisted-packet roundtrip with 3,617 IDs.

Final CLI run exited 0. Seven checks passed: valid roundtrip; wrong tokenizer profile; wrong render profile; tampered IDs; negative ID; unexpected input; and rehashed wrong text. Wrong profiles, tampered IDs, invalid ID and unexpected source were rejected before decode. Rehashed wrong text was rejected after decoding but before return.
The two tokenizer JSON files differ in added_tokens, but their ID sequences for this exact input are equal. This limits conclusions about tokenizer diversity.

Executed with /Users/alexey.zhuchkov/Documents/Agents/.venv/bin/python /private/tmp/accord-token-probe.py. Reads only tokenizer JSON and the supplied input; writes only /private/tmp artifacts; loads no model weights and invokes no inference engine or network API.

artifacts.purpose: Runnable local probe and focused integrity/profile tests.
Measurements, hashes, exact roundtrip results and seven actual check outcomes.
Exact worker result envelope for parent validation.

checks.name: Exact source hashes, serialization measurements and byte-for-byte roundtrip for two tokenizer profiles
Seven focused transport integrity, profile mismatch and source binding checks
Compare actual tokenizer artifacts and ID sequences
Model inference, native agent token-ID messaging, billing, inference latency or quality measurement

limitations: Both cached directories belong to embedding models. Only tokenizer JSON was loaded; these results do not test a chat model or its API.
Distinct tokenizer hashes produced identical IDs for this input; the experiment does not establish portability across unrelated tokenizers.
The input is already-rendered worker-context text, with no chat template, role framing, tools or engine request. Native agent tools accept text; no token-ID messages were sent.
Hashes provide integrity binding to separately supplied expected values, not sender authentication. A party able to replace both an artifact and its trusted expectations can forge the hashes.

Token IDs preserve an encoding of the prompt text; they do not compile its semantics or represent inference/KV-cache state. No billing, inference latency, quality or KV-cache-saving claim follows from these byte measurements.
All created files are temporary experimental artifacts under /private/tmp; no production or repository files were changed.
